title: Expose internal publish API for quantization profiles + publisher permission checks
author: Quentin Harris
description:
Context: Quantization Profile Library v1 needs a server-side publish surface (internal-only) so Applied ML can add/update Redwood-published quantization profiles in the registry with consistent validation + audit. This PR exposes internal publish endpoints and adds permission checks aligned with the restricted publisher workflow.

What’s included: 1) New internal endpoints for publishing quantization profiles. Supports create + update with semantic version enforcement and hardware scoping validation. 2) Server-side validation: profile JSON schema validation, manifest layout checks (per PR #912 conventions), kernel/hardware scope format validation, and immutable fields enforcement (model_id, profile_id). 3) Permissioning: enforce service auth + RBAC gate for publish operations (requires model-registry.quant_profiles.publish). Adds dedicated publisher allowlist group mapping for Applied ML (per INT-1934) and denies all customer identities. 4) Auditability: audit log entries for publish attempts (success + deny), including requester identity, profile_id, model_id, version, and artifact digest.

Endpoints (internal): POST /internal/v1/quantization-profiles:publish — create new profile version (server allocates canonical artifact path + writes manifest pointer); PUT /internal/v1/quantization-profiles/{profile_id}:publish — update metadata for an existing profile_id (restricted fields) + publish new version; POST /internal/v1/quantization-profiles:validate — dry-run validation returning structured error codes (used by CI + tooling).

Notes: This is not customer-facing. This does not yet implement signature verification for uploaded artifacts; signing is performed by the publishing pipeline after upload and before the registry marks a version as “available” (follow-up in security thread). The endpoints are designed to be called by the internal publish job in eval-harness/CI.

Rollout: guarded behind INTERNAL_PUBLISH_API_ENABLED (default on in staging, off in prod until Applied ML pipeline is ready). Once enabled, requests must present service-to-service auth + RBAC claim; Console/gateway tokens will be rejected.

Testing: unit tests for RBAC checks and validation errors; integration test for happy-path publish with manifest layout from #912; regression tests for version monotonicity and immutable fields.

Checklist: [x] Linked to ENG-18420 and INT-1934 approval trail [x] Added audit log events [x] Added docs in internal API README [x] Added error code mapping for platform callers [x] Verified staging publish with a synthetic profile (llama-3.1-8b-int8) against A100 scope
commits: api: add internal quantization profile publish + validate routes
authz: add quant profile publisher RBAC gate + deny customer principals
validation: enforce schema + manifest layout (PR #912) + semver monotonicity
audit: emit publish_attempt / publish_denied / publish_succeeded events
tests: integration fixture for publish; error code snapshots
docs: internal endpoints + examples for publish job
review_conversation: Priya Natarajan (Platform): Can we make sure the validate endpoint returns stable machine-readable codes? Platform will need to map these into a publish PR comment + gating signal. Also please confirm we don’t leak filesystem paths in error payloads.
Quentin Harris (Author): Added error_code + error_path fields and scrubbed internal storage paths. validate now returns {code, message, field} entries only. Included snapshot tests.

Marcus Lin (Security): The RBAC gate is good, but we need to ensure customer tokens can’t reach these routes even if misconfigured upstream. Can we require service auth header + internal audience claim?
Quentin Harris (Author): Updated middleware to require svc-auth + aud=registry-internal for /internal/* routes. Added a deny test for API keys and Console JWTs.

Mateo Alvarez (Runtime): Please ensure immutable fields include kernel_family constraints; we don’t want publish updates to silently broaden a profile scope without re-validation. Also do we have a clear rule about version monotonicity vs overwrite?

Quentin Harris (Author): Enforced immutable: model_id, profile_id, quant_method, kernel_family. Scope broadening requires a new semver minor and passes full validation. Overwrite is disallowed; only publish new versions. Added explicit 409 QUANT_PROFILE_VERSION_EXISTS.
Jordan Lee (Policy): For audit logs, can we include org_id when present even though this is internal? Helps correlate if someone accidentally forwards a request. Also include request_id for tracing.
Quentin Harris (Author): Included org_id when present (it’s usually null) and always include request_id + actor_id. Added to audit schema.
Arjun Desai (Applied ML): This matches what we need for the publish job. Can you add an example request body that includes calibration_notes + expected_speedup fields? The team will copy/paste.
Quentin Harris (Author): Added examples section to docs/internal_api.md with a realistic payload. Also added validate example with common failure modes.
Priya Natarajan (Platform): Approved once lint is green.
CI Bot: lint — FAIL (unused import in publish_service.ts)
merge_outcome: Merged via squash into main by Quentin Harris on 2025-01-17. Follow-ups: add artifact signing verification gate before marking versions available; wire eval-harness publish job to use validate + publish; add rate limiting on internal publish to protect registry during bulk backfills.
